findings: lem:pushup_local (ETT.tex:557-560) holds with 'causally arc-connected' replaced by 'absolutely minimal' on every T1 space, hence on every topological spacetime of the paper (Hausdorff, def:category_topological_spacetimes, ETT.tex:254-255). The paper's proof (ETT.tex:561-583) uses causal arc-connectedness twice: to cut the last segment of a chronal curve inside U_i (the one-step claim, ETT.tex:566-572) and to subdivide a causal curve along the cover (ETT.tex:575-582). Absolute minimality gives both without curves: the causal chain is the expansion of y ≤_U z over the cover by the U_i, and the last chronological step into z is localised in U_i by expanding y ≪ z over the two-set cover {U_i, M ∖ {z}}, open by T1 (Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn.exists_lt_inf_last). Both clauses of defi:pushup (ETT.tex:307-312) are proved, the second by time reversal.

Comparison with the sibling edges AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture and .causallyOpen_of_locallyCausallyOpen (Causal/LadderLocal.lean; prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal, ETT.tex:698-701): those need no separation axiom, because J⁺_U(V) is reached through ≤-chains alone and openness propagates along the expansion of ≤ over any cover. Push-up mixes ≪ and ≤, and the step needs the last ≪-step to land in the push-up neighbourhood of its end point, which absolute minimality grants only against a cover in which that neighbourhood is the one member containing the end point: this is where T1 enters, and it cannot be removed (label 3).

hypotheses.paper: the planner: 'under the gluing reading of defi:causalite (every causality absolutely minimal) the local and global forms of push-up and of causal openness coincide on T1 spaces'
hypotheses.note: proved as implications from AbsolutelyMinimal: push-up ⇔ local push-up asks T1; causal openness ⇔ local causal openness (future form and DEC-8 two-sided form) asks no separation axiom. The gluing reading itself is not formalised: it is OQ-18

findings: For OQ-67 (b) and OQ-18 (the master's to record, not a ruling): if defi:causalite is read with gluing, so that every causality is absolutely minimal (kb/0014), then on T1 spaces locally_push_up ⇔ push_up, and outright locally_causally_open_future ⇔ causally_open_future and locally_causally_open ⇔ causally_open. The ladder's separations locally_push_up ⇏ push_up (the gated line, Causal.gateLine_separates_pushUp) and locally_causally_open ⇏ causally_open / locally_causally_open_future ⇏ causally_open_future (the jump and gated lines) therefore hold only in the reading without gluing; they are not separations between ETT spacetimes in the gluing reading. By contrast the half-chronological line's separations (label 4) hold in either reading.

hypotheses.paper: a witness that the standing T1 cannot be dropped
hypotheses.note: the vee: points left, mid, right; open sets ∅, {mid}, {left, mid}, {mid, right}, the whole space (T0, not T1: {mid} is not closed); x ≤_U y iff x, y ∈ U and x ≤ y in left < mid < right; x ≪_U y iff left ∈ U, x ≠ right, y = mid. Absolutely minimal (every cover contains {left, mid} or the whole space, and {mid, right} or the whole space); push-up on {left, mid} and, vacuously, on {mid, right}; left ≪ mid ≤ right and nothing is ≪ right

findings: T1 cannot be dropped from absolutely_minimal ∧ locally_push_up ⇒ push_up, nor weakened to T0 (Causal.not_pushUp_of_absolutelyMinimal_of_locallyPushUp_T0). The vee is not Hausdorff, so it is not a topological spacetime of the paper (ETT.tex:255): it shows the sharpness of the edge's standing only, and says nothing on ETT's spacetimes. It is also the first absolutely minimal causality in Lean without push-up, on a non-T1 space.

hypotheses.paper: a witness that local push-up cannot be dropped (beyond the target: the sharpness of its second premise)
hypotheses.note: Causal.halfChronoLine (Causal/LinesReachable.lean:236): the timelike line's ≤, and x ≪_U y iff -1 < x < y and [x, y] ⊆ U. Push-up fails in every open containing -1: -1 ≤ y ≪ z without -1 ≪ z. Causally arc-connected: ≤ and causal curves are the timelike line's; p ≪_U q forces p > -1 and the affine curve from p stays after p. GH, causal, strongly causal, causally open, tarentin by definitional equality with the timelike line (kb/0052); strong causality in the open form by StronglyCausal.stronglyCausalOpen; time function id; curves extend (re-proved: CausalCurveIn is indexed by the causality)

findings: lem:pushup_local (ETT.tex:557-560) needs its cover by push-up opens even on a causally arc-connected, globally hyperbolic, strongly causal, causally open, tarentin spacetime with a time function: the half-chronological line on ℝ has all of these and is neither locally push-up nor push-up. Being causally arc-connected it is absolutely minimal, so this holds in either reading of defi:causalite (OQ-18). Among the ladder's witnesses it is the first lacking local push-up (the [[open]] notes on X → locally_push_up read 'no Lean model lacks local push-up') and the first absolutely minimal one without push-up (the comment above the [[implies]] absolutely_minimal ∧ causally_plain ⇒ push_up in programme/ladder.toml: 'no Lean model is absolutely minimal without push-up'). It is not causally plain (halfChronoLine_not_causallyPlain, Causal/LinesReachable.lean:292), as the edge absolutely_minimal ∧ causally_plain ⇒ push_up (T1) requires of such a witness, and it has no chronal neighbours (halfChronoLine_not_chronalNeighbours).

kb_proposals: On a T1 space absolute minimality localises the LAST step of a chronological chain in any open containing its end point (Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn.exists_lt_inf_last, the time reversal of exists_lt_inf); with the expansion of ≤ over a cover it turns local push-up into push-up (Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal.pushUp_of_locallyPushUp). T1 is necessary: the three-point vee (Causal.veeCausality_separates_pushUp) (T-abs-pushup-of-minimal-local).

The half-chronological line (Causal.halfChronoLine, chronology only after -1) is the cheap ETT spacetime without local push-up: causally arc-connected, GH, strongly causal, causally open, tarentin, a time function, curves extend; push-up fails in every neighbourhood of -1 (Causal.halfChronoLine_separates_pushUp). Use it before building a non-local witness for a separation into push_up or locally_push_up (T-abs-pushup-of-minimal-local).
